hook.situation: Arranging a meeting time, counting items, reading dates, asking prices, and talking about age without mixing the two Korean number systems.
objectives: Use native Korean numbers for hours and common counters: 한 시, 두 잔, 세 명.
Use Sino-Korean numbers for minutes, dates, prices, phone-style numbers, and floors: 십 분, 이월 삼일, 오천 원.
Recognize common number questions: 몇 시, 몇 분, 몇 잔, 얼마예요, 나이가 어떻게 되세요?
hook.whyItMatters: Korean numbers are not random; the object being counted chooses the number family. Once learners know the common pairings, time, prices, dates, and simple shopping conversations become much more predictable.

grammarNotes.title: Two number systems: native (하나·둘·셋) vs. Sino-Korean (일·이·삼)
grammarNotes.func: Korean has two full sets of numbers, and which one you use depends on what you're saying — not on which you like better. Native numbers count things, people, and the o'clock hour. Sino-Korean numbers handle money, minutes, dates, and phone numbers. The clock uses both at once: native for the hour, Sino for the minute.

formTable.when: Counting things, people, or animals (with a counter)
formTable.add: Native 하나·둘·셋·넷, but 1–4 shorten before a counter → 한·두·세·네
formTable.ex: 사과 한 개 (one apple), 친구 두 명 (two friends)

formTable.add: Native number + 시 (1–4 shorten here too)
formTable.ex: 세 시 (3 o'clock), 네 시 (4 o'clock)
삼십 분 (30 minutes), 오천 원 (5,000 won)

formTable.add: Native + 살 in daily talk; Sino + 세 on official forms
formTable.ex: 스무 살 (20 years old, everyday), 이십 세 (on forms)

examples.note: Counting a thing, so native — and 하나 shortens to 한 before the counter 병.
The hour 시 takes native 세, but the minute 분 takes Sino 삼십 — both systems in one time.
Money is always Sino (오천), never 다섯천.

examples.ko: 우리 반에 학생이 열 명 있어요.
examples.romanization: uri ban-e haksaeng-i yeol myeong isseoyo.
examples.en: There are ten students in our class.
examples.note: Counting people with 명, so native 열 — and 열 keeps its shape; only 한·두·세·네 and 스무 change.

keyPoint.label: The clock uses both systems
keyPoint.body: The hour (시) is native: 한 시, 두 시, 세 시. The minute (분) is Sino: 일 분, 십 분, 삼십 분. So 3:20 is 세 시 이십 분 — native for the hour, Sino for the minute. If you can remember this one phrase, you've got the whole rule. (Which counter goes with which number is a later topic; for now just lock in hour vs. minute.)

grammarNotes.pronunciation: 여섯 개 sounds like [여섣 깨] and 일곱 시 like [일곱 씨] — the counter's first consonant tenses after the number's final consonant. Also remember the short forms before a counter: 하나→한, 둘→두, 셋→세, 넷→네, 스물→스무.

drill.instruction: Say each one out loud, picking the right number system and the right form before the counter.

englishSpeakerPitfall.explanation: In English one set of numbers does everything, so it's tempting to grab the more familiar Sino 삼 for '3 o'clock.' But the hour is always native: 세 시. The flip side of the same habit is reaching for native 다섯 to say money (다섯천 원) instead of Sino 오천 원. Quick check before you speak: am I counting things or hours (native), or saying money, minutes, or a date (Sino)?

exampleSentence.note: Before many counters, 하나 becomes 한: 한 개, 한 명, 한 시.

exampleSentence.en: Please give me two cups of coffee.
I have class at three o'clock.

exampleSentence.note: Use 일 with minutes, dates, prices, floors, and phone-style numbers.

exampleSentence.en: I am going to Korea in February.
exampleSentence.note: Use 이 for Sino-Korean number settings such as months and prices.
Use 삼 in prices, dates, and minutes, but not for clock hour three.
몇 combines with a counter or number unit: 몇 시, 몇 분, 몇 명, 몇 개.
Clock hours use native numbers before 시.
시간 can mean available time or duration, so context matters.
Prices use Sino-Korean numbers before 원.
In shops, 이거 얼마예요? is often more natural than saying 가격 every time.
Dates use Sino-Korean numbers with 월 and 일.
생일 questions often lead to month and day practice.

exampleSentence.en: May I ask how old you are?
exampleSentence.note: Use this polite formula with adults; actual age uses native numbers with 살.

extendedDialogue.setting: Friends arrange a meeting time and check prices before buying coffee and a birthday cake.

lines.speaker: 민서
lines.grammarNote: 몇 시 asks for clock time.

lines.speaker: 지훈
lines.ko: 세 시 십 분에 지하철역 앞에서 만나요.
lines.romanization: se si sip bune jihacheoryeok apeseo mannayo.
lines.en: Let's meet at 3:10 in front of the subway station.
lines.grammarNote: 세 is native for the hour; 십 is Sino-Korean for the minutes.

lines.speaker: 민서
lines.en: How many cups of coffee should we buy?

lines.speaker: 지훈
lines.ko: 두 잔이면 돼요. 한 잔에 이천오백 원이에요.
lines.romanization: du janimyeon dwaeyo. han jane icheonobaek wonieyo.
lines.en: Two cups are enough. One cup is 2,500 won.
lines.grammarNote: 두 잔 uses a native number; 이천오백 원 uses Sino-Korean numbers.

lines.speaker: 민서
lines.grammarNote: Price totals use Sino-Korean numbers before 원.

lines.speaker: 지훈
lines.ko: 네. 생일 케이크는 만 이천 원이에요.
lines.romanization: ne. saengil keikeuneun man icheon wonieyo.
lines.en: Yes. The birthday cake is 12,000 won.

readingText.title: A birthday meet-up
readingText.body: 민서와 지훈은 토요일에 친구 생일을 준비해요. 두 사람은 세 시 십 분에 지하철역 앞에서 만나기로 했어요. 커피는 두 잔을 사고, 한 잔에 이천오백 원이라서 모두 오천 원이에요. 케이크는 만 이천 원이에요. 민서는 예약 날짜도 확인했어요. 생일은 이월 삼일이고, 케이크는 토요일 네 시 전에 찾을 수 있어요. 그래서 두 사람은 시간과 가격을 다시 확인하고 가게에 갔어요.
readingText.bodyTranslation: Minseo and Jihoon prepare for a friend's birthday on Saturday. They plan to meet at 3:10, buy two coffees, check the cake price, confirm the birthday date, and pick up the cake before 4:00.

comprehensionQuestions.question: 민서와 지훈은 몇 시 십 분에 만나기로 했어요?
comprehensionQuestions.answer: 세 시 십 분에 만나기로 했어요.

culturalNote.title: Age and price both need register awareness
culturalNote.body: Prices are easy to ask directly with 얼마예요? Age is more sensitive. With adults or people you do not know well, 나이가 어떻게 되세요? is safer than 몇 살이에요?, which can sound childish or too direct.
culturalNote.tip: Use 얼마예요? freely for prices, but be careful with age questions unless the situation clearly calls for it.

inlineExercises.prompt: Which time expression is natural for 3:10?
inlineExercises.explanation: Hours use native Korean numbers; minutes use Sino-Korean numbers.
Use native 한 for the hour and Sino-Korean 오 for the minutes.
Prices use Sino-Korean numbers before 원.

inlineExercises.prompt: Fix the sentence: 삼 시 십 분에 만나요.
inlineExercises.explanation: Clock hour three is 세 시, not 삼 시.

inlineExercises.prompt: Fix the age sentence: 저는 이십 살이에요.
inlineExercises.explanation: Age uses native Korean numbers with 살; 스물 becomes 스무 before the counter.

inlineExercises.prompt: 커피 두 잔___ 주세요. (Please give me two cups of coffee.)
inlineExercises.explanation: 두 잔 is the counted object being requested, so 을 fits when the particle is shown. In casual ordering, Koreans often drop it, but 을 is the grammatical object marker.
Hours use native Korean numbers, so 3 o’clock is 세 시. Minutes use Sino-Korean numbers, so 10 minutes is 십 분.
잔 is a cup/glass counter and takes native Korean numbers. Two cups is 두 잔, not 이 잔.

inlineExercises.prompt: Which price expression is natural for 3,000 won?
inlineExercises.explanation: Prices use Sino-Korean numbers, so 3,000 won is 삼천 원. 세 and 셋 are native forms and do not fit this price expression.

bullets: Hours and common counters use native numbers: 한 시, 두 잔, 세 명.
Minutes, dates, and prices use Sino-Korean numbers: 십 분, 이월 삼일, 오천 원.
몇 attaches to the unit you need: 몇 시, 몇 분, 몇 잔, 몇 명.
Age is socially sensitive: use 나이가 어떻게 되세요? before jumping to 몇 살이에요?

writingTask.prompt: Write 3 sentences telling a friend the time you'll meet, the price of a coffee, and how many people are coming.
writingTask.hint: Use Sino-Korean numbers for minutes/price (세 시 삼십 분, 사천 원) and native numbers for the hour and counting people (세 시, 네 명).
writingTask.model: 우리 세 시 삼십 분에 만나요. 커피는 사천 원이에요. 친구 네 명이 와요.
writingTask.modelEn: Let's meet at 3:30. The coffee is 4,000 won. Four friends are coming.

canDo: Tell the o'clock hour with native numbers (세 시 · 네 시)
Say minutes and prices with Sino-Korean numbers (삼십 분 · 사천 원)
Count people and things with native numbers plus a counter (네 명)
Ask "how many / how much" with 몇 and 얼마 (몇 시 · 얼마예요?)
